subject: Request: Erase verification artifacts and proof for SOC2/ISO audit
messages:
From: auditor@brightline-audit.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Evidence needed: tenant erase verification and retention mapping (Clearwater)

Hi Naomi,

We are conducting the fieldwork for Clearwater Bank's SOC2 readiness review. The scope includes tenant lifecycle: residency, retention, and deletion controls for tenant CLW-9876. Please provide the following artifacts by EOD Nov 30 so we can validate the control implementation: 

1) Erase verification certificate or signed attestation showing deletion runs for CLW-9876 (date range Jul 2025 - Nov 2026)
2) S3 lifecycle report / object counts showing objects transitioned/expired with timestamps and bucket names
3) KMS key rotation and deletion logs tied to the tenant keys (key ids acceptable)
4) Runbook excerpts that describe the deletion process and any manual escalation steps
5) A sample manifest (CSV) from a deletion job showing object identifiers and resulting tombstone entries

If any of these are covered by previously produced artifacts, point us to the link. If you anticipate a delay, let us know a revised ETA.

Thanks,
Rachel Park
Senior Auditor | Brightline Audit
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: auditor@brightline-audit.com, compliance@clearwater.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-25T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence needed: tenant erase verification and retention mapping (Clearwater)

Hi Rachel / Clearwater team,

Thanks for the detailed list — we can provide these artifacts. High-level plan and constraints below: 

- We will produce an "erase verification attestation" (PDF) summarizing deletion runs for CLW-9876 and include run IDs + timestamps.
- S3 lifecycle exports: we'll provide a bucket/object-level CSV extract for the buckets that host tenant blobs. Note that object-level identifiers are hashed for privacy; we'll include a mapping file for auditors under NDA.
- KMS logs: we can provide key rotation events and OP logs for the tenant-specific CMK (redacted key ids in external copies).
- Runbook excerpts: policy + steps for automated TTL jobs and manual remediation steps; we'll annotate the sections that apply to tenant deletions.
- Sample manifest: small CSV sample (non-production object ids replaced with pseudonyms) showing tombstone entries and job exit codes.

Vivek / Karthik — can you confirm we can package the above and attach the sample files? Target is Nov 30 EOD PST. If any item requires legal review (export of key metadata), flag it now.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Compliance | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-26T08:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence needed: tenant erase verification and retention mapping (Clearwater)

Naomi — quick notes from runtime/security perspective: 

- Deletion jobs are run nightly as TTL sweep jobs (service: lifecycle-sweeper). We retain job logs for 12 months in our audit index and snapshots for 36 months in cold storage. For CLW-9876, we have runs labeled "sweeper-clw-9876-<date>".
- We can produce a crosswalk: sweep run id -> affected prefix -> object count -> job exit code. We'll redact full object keys in the shared CSV and include SHA256 hashes of object keys for traceability.
- KMS: tenant uses a customer-bound data key (CBK-CLW-9876) wrapped by a platform CMK. We will provide rotation events (timestamp + version) and tombstone/disable events for the CBK if present. Note: raw KMS ciphertext is sensitive; we will only provide event metadata.
- Escalation play: if a sweep finds protected flag set, job creates a ticket in JIRA (SUP-3142) and pauses deletion pending manual review. We'll include the runbook snippet and an anonymized ticket example.

I will prepare the S3 lifecycle export and a sample sweep manifest. Karthik, can you export the TTL mapping spreadsheet and the runbook excerpt?

— Vivek
Head of Security Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-29T11:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence needed: tenant erase verification and retention mapping (Clearwater)

Team,

I've pulled the exports and attached the working artifacts to this thread (internal copy):
- s3-lifecycle-report-tenant-CLW-9876.csv (columns: bucket, prefix, last_modified, lifecycle_action, transition_date, expiry_date, object_count)
- kv-cache-ttl-mapping.xlsx (mapping of services -> TTL default -> per-tenant overrides)
- runbook-delete-excerpt.md (excerpt with flowchart and manual steps)
- sample-sweep-manifest.csv (run_id, hashed_object_id, tombstone_ts, exit_code)

Notes: the sample manifest contains hashed_object_id (sha256) for each object; auditors can validate consistency by hashing an object id they provide under NDA. For the attestation PDF, Naomi — do you want to sign with your director stamp or legal prefers a different template? I attached an erase-cert-template.pdf (internal).

Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Data Infra | Redwood Inference

- erase-verification-attestation-CLW-9876.pdf (signed by Naomi Feldman, Director, Customer Compliance)

Access and notes:

- KMS rotation/disable events (metadata only) are included in the attached attestation appendix. We cannot share raw ciphertext or key material; this is standard for platform KMS usage.
- For traceability, we included sweep run ids and job exit codes. You can use the SHA256 hash to confirm consistency if you provide a sample object id under NDA.

If you need anything further (for example, an expanded timespan or raw logs on a secure pull), let us know — we can coordinate with legal to set up a secure transfer.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
